farhi-qnn-readout-prediction: Sec. 1, p.3, Eq. 5: the paper defines its predicted label as the expectation of Y on the readout qubit, the average of repeated outcomes.
farhi-sample-loss-linear: Sec. 1, p.3, Eq. 6: the loss is the paper's own definition. Linear in the margin and bounded below by 0 follow directly from it and the stated bound on the predicted label.
farhi-no-explicit-nonlinearity: Sec. 1, p.4: the paper states the structure of its own network, a chain of unitaries with no explicit non-linearity.
farhi-open-compact-representation: Sec. 2, p.6: the authors state this as an open area of investigation about their own framework, a stated limit of what the paper settles.
farhi-subset-majority-representation: Sec. 2.1, p.7, Eq. 17 to 21, and Sec. 3.2, p.11: for an odd subset, with beta = 0.9 pi / n the argument of the sine has magnitude below pi, so the sign matches the majority. The derivation is in the paper and the condition (odd size) is in the quotes.
farhi-exact-gradient-simulation: Sec. 3, p.9: the paper states how its own simulations compute the gradient, exactly and without finite differences, and why the size is small (Hilbert space dimension 2 to the n + 1).
farhi-mnist-setup: Sec. 3.3, p.12: the paper states its dataset choice (4 by 4 downsampled MNIST, digits 3 and 6) and the simulator size reason.
farhi-mnist-ambiguous-removal: Sec. 3.3, p.12: the paper states its own data preparation counts (797, 617, 197, 3514, 2517, 6031). 3514 + 2517 = 6031 checks.
farhi-mnist-no-gate-guidance: Sec. 3.3, p.12-13: the authors state they have little guidance on circuit design, a limit on their own work, and hope to find principles for gate sets. Its result_type is better read as a limit than as a setup.
farhi-superposition-test-contamination: Sec. 3.4, p.14: the authors state their test strings were included in the superposition states, a flaw in their own protocol.
farhi-superposition-preparation-cost: Sec. 4, p.18: the authors state that classical data must be read into a device to prepare the superposition and that the superposition is consumed, so fresh copies are needed. It is a stated cost of their own protocol.
farhi-state-label-classical-description: Sec. 3.5, p.17: the authors state a caution about their own test states, which have a classical description so a classical competitor is conceivable.
farhi-no-advantage-claim: Sec. 4, p.19: the authors state that their numerics cannot make a case for quantum advantage. A limit on their own work; the result_type should be a limit, not a setup.
farhi-simulation-size-limit: Sec. 4, p.19: the authors state they worked at no more than 17 qubits and that 40 qubits would need more resources. A limit on their own work.
exploratory-no-scaling: Sec. 3.3, p.13: the authors state the data set could easily be classified by a classical network, that a fixed low bit number precludes any discussion of scaling, and that the work is exploratory. All three are limits on their own work.
exponentially-long-circuit-some-labels: The narrowed value matches the passage. Abstract says 'is exponentially long', Sec. 2 p.5 says the formula 'can be exponentially long', Sec. 2 p.6 and Sec. 4 p.17 say 'may need to be'. The paper states this as a limit of its own construction; it does not prove a lower bound for every circuit.
qgat-contribution: Sec. 1, p.2: the paper states what it proposes (QGAT) and its implementation (PyTorch, Qadence).
qgat-attention-layer-definition: Sec. 4.1, p.5: the paper defines the state |F(x alpha)> as the quantum attention layer.
qgat-attention-weights-scale-features: Sec. 4.1, p.5: the paper's own model definition, where the neighbor feature is weighted by its coefficient before the feature map.
qgat-qgcn-w-gates: Sec. 4.2, p.5-6: the paper states its own circuit composition for W (3 CZ, 3 rotations, 4 RG gates), using the decomposition of [40] as a design choice. It is a setup, not a result.
qgat-pooling-halves-qubits: Sec. 4.2, p.6: the paper states its own pooling design, half the qubits traced out per step, and its choice of deferred measurement.
qgat-same-circuit-any-neighbor-count: Sec. 4.3, p.6: a stated property of the paper's own model, the same QGCN for any neighbor count.
qgat-qm9-task: Sec. 2, p.3: the paper states how it frames its task on QM9.
qgat-qm9-features: Sec. 2, p.3 and footnote 1: the paper lists its seven features and the four it omits as zero in its samples.
qgat-training-details: Sec. 5.1, p.7: the paper states loss, score, optimizer and learning rate for its own experiments.
qgat-algorithm-hops: Sec. 5.1, p.7-8: the paper states its own algorithm, all hops up to the atom count, and a single-branch graph with one head.
qgat-feature-map-observable: Sec. 5.1, p.8: the paper states its own encoding and measurement (Eq. 20, local magnetization with tunable weights).
qgat-sample-size: Sec. 5.2, p.8 and the Table 1 caption: the paper states the samples per subset (30 or 40) and the metrics, as its own protocol.
qgat-table1-params: Table 1, p.8: parameter counts 209, 218, 1675, 1700 match the rows (classical 30, quantum 30, classical multi 40, quantum multi 40).
qgat-setup: Sec. 5.1, p.8: the paper states 8 inputs or qubits (7 features plus one for the mean self-embedding) and its frameworks (PyTorch, Qadence).
farias-scope: Abstract and Sec. I, p.1: the review states its own scope, qudits in QML with focus on VQAs and QNNs.
farias-qudit-definition: Sec. II, p.1: the paper defines a qudit as a system with d orthogonal basis states, generalizing the qubit.
fedorov-scope-review: Abstract, p.1: the review states its own coverage and style.
fedorov-universal-vs-nonuniversal: Sec. V, p.7-8: the paper defines universal and non-universal devices, lists the four universal models and the two non-universal classes, and states the Turing machine extension (Deutsch 1985 [34]).
fedorov-error-rate-definition: Sec. VI, p.14: the paper defines the error rate epsilon as the ratio of gate duration to characteristic decoherence time, and says the overhead depends on it.
fedorov-software-three-levels: Sec. X, p.36: 'We identify three levels of quantum software', each defined by its platform and model dependence, with the last handled by hardware makers.
feng-scope-three-models: Sec. I, p.2 and Sec. II.A, p.2: the paper states the three models it studies and its primary focus.
feng-xorx-scar-sequence: Sec. II.A p.2 and II.C p.4: the paper states the model's scar sequence with m at most n over 2, and the conserved domain wall number with the identity shown in the text.
feng-fig2-setup: Figure 2 caption, p.3: the paper states its own simulation parameters (12 spins, two boundary spins fixed, lambda = J = 10 Delta).
feng-quasiparticle-approximate: Sec. II.C.2, p.5: the authors state their quasiparticle picture is only approximate and the quasiparticles are more intricate. A limit on their own result.
feng-hardware-setup: Sec. II.D p.7 and Appendix B p.13: the paper states training by noise-free classical simulation, then the run on IBM hanoi on the exact state S1, with a CNOT error of about 1%.
feng-hardware-groups: Figure 10 caption, p.7: the paper states 12 groups spaced hours apart. The text prints 104 repeats, which is 10^4 with the exponent flat; the value already says so.
feng-mitigation-methods: Sec. II.D, p.7: the paper states its two mitigation methods and the assumption of error 1 + 2r times that of U.
feng-fidelity-proxy: Appendix B, p.13: the authors state their own approximations (all-zero state fidelity as a proxy, single-qubit errors neglected, zeroth-order Eq. B2). These are limits on their own method; its type should be a limit, not a setup.
feng-drift-groups: Appendix B, p.13: the paper states why it organized the experiments in groups at different times.
feng-open-analytic-understanding: Sec. II.E, p.9: the authors state that an analytical understanding of the PXP and SSH non-thermal states is an open problem. A limit on their own work.
feng-qcnn-architecture: Sec. IV.A, p.10: the paper states its own QCNN design (brickwall layers with shared parameters, pooling by measurement, extra layers, general layers and an ancilla).
feng-loss-function: Sec. IV.B, p.10, Eq. 11 (checked on the rendered page): L = (1/d) times the sum of |y_i - q_i|, with the labels as stated.
feng-marked-threshold: Sec. IV.B, p.10: the paper defines a marked eigenstate as one with output above 50% and states the majority vote used in experiment.
feng-preprocess-fixed-depth: Appendix A, p.12: the paper states its own design choice, a pre-processing circuit of fixed depth independent of qubit number.

theory_low.farhi-gradient-bounded: Sec. 1, p.4-5: a two-sentence informal argument, not a stated and proved result. It says the derivative operator has norm at most 1 and then asserts the loss gradient is bounded by L, with no derivation of how the loss gradient follows.
theory_low.farhi-representation-any-label: Sec. 2, p.5-6: the abstract step (Eq. 9 to 11) is shown, but the claim is about a circuit of two qubit unitaries, and that step rests on the cited result [11] (Barenco et al.), which the paper takes without proof.
theory_low.farhi-representation-two-qubit-count: Sec. 2, p.6: the order n squared two qubit unitaries per controlled operation is taken from early work [11] (Barenco et al.), cited not proved. The text layer also prints n squared as n2.
theory_low.farhi-subset-parity-representation: Sec. 2.1, p.6: the quantum half (at most n commuting two qubit operators, from Eq. 16) follows from the paper's construction. The classical half, three layers needed on a standard network, is stated without proof and rests on the cited classical representation results [12][13]. Graded by the weaker half.
theory_low.farhi-measurements-needed: Sec. 3, p.8: the 2 over delta squared measurement count is stated with no derivation and no named inequality. A standard concentration bound, but the paper does not prove it.
theory_low.farhi-finite-difference-cost: Sec. 3, p.8: a short informal scaling argument (error order eta needs about 1 over eta cubed measurements), stated as 'of order', not a proved bound.
theory_low.farhi-aux-qubit-gradient: Sec. 3, p.8-9: the strategy is credited to [14] (Romero et al.). Eq. 23 is stated without derivation, and the depth 2L + 2 count is asserted, not derived for the controlled circuit.
theory_low.farhi-parity-unlearnable-large-n: Sec. 3.1, p.10: an argument for one case (n a multiple of 4, S all bits) that the authors label 'we now argue'. The empirical risk formula (Eq. 35) is given without derivation, and 'impossible to learn' is an interpretation. No theorem is stated.
theory_low.farhi-parity-doomed-large-n: Sec. 3.1, p.11: the authors apply the result of [15] (Shalev-Shwartz et al.) to their case by saying the parity functions are orthonormal. It is a cited result applied by assertion, not proved in this paper.
theory_low.farhi-state-label-representation: Sec. 3.5, p.15-16, Eq. 42 to 45: an informal argument. Eq. 44 gives the expectation of sin(2 beta H), then the paper says it is 'close to' 2 beta times the expectation of H for small beta. No bound is given, and for states with the expectation of H near zero the sign can differ. The paper itself says only that the error can be made small.
theory_low.farias-qutrit-bits: Sec. II, p.1: the paper prints log2 3 as about 1.53. The true value is about 1.585, so the paper's own number is wrong. Stated without derivation as a field statement, with citations [4] to [7].
theory_low.fedorov-variational-universality-open: Sec. V.D, p.10-11: the limit is on the universality proofs of other groups (Lloyd, Biamonte, refs [78-80]), which are cited. This review states no limit on its own work, so it is not a stated limit.
theory_low.fedorov-quantum-volume-example: Box 8, p.16: a worked illustration with N = 10^6 and epsilon = 10^-3, optimal n about 30 (n = 1/(n epsilon) gives about 32). It is an example, not a stated result with conditions.
theory_low.feng-ancilla-necessity: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix A, p.12-13 gives a one sentence dimension argument (a unitary does not change the Hilbert space size) with no proof.
